source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) – Členové (member banks directory)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of ~34 banks and building societies covering >99% of the CZ banking sector. This is the canonical buyer-universe list for A2 tender monitoring: every entity here is a potential contracting entity (some are also sectoral/state-linked buyers) and the list lets us seed profile/entity resolution against tender portals. Note www.cbaonline.cz/o-nas/clenove also appears in search indexes as an alternative path.

source_name: ČLFA – Seznam členských společností (leasing & consumer finance members)
source_subtype: association member directory with per-member pages
why_relevant: ~35 leasing/consumer-finance companies (Ayvens, Arval, Bibby, captive OEM finance arms). These are non-bank financial buyers of POS/payment/IT services that keyword tender searches rarely surface; each member has its own detail page on clfa.cz, giving structured company records.

source_name: Finance.cz – mirror listing of ČLFA members (seznamy a adresáře)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator mirror of the ČLFA roster; useful as a redundancy/cross-check source when the association site is restructured, and it sits inside a broader 'seznamy a adresáře' directory hub that points at further financial-sector lists.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace (Czech Fintech Association) – Členové
why_relevant: 80+ members/affiliates spanning payment gateways (GoPay, ComGate), card/POS tech (Aevi, MONET+, Wultra), data (CRIF, Dateio) and consultancies (Deloitte). This is the highest-yield map of the CZ payments supplier long tail — i.e. our competitor and partner universe when reading award notices. Bilingual site (cs/en).

source_name: Svaz průmyslu a dopravy ČR (SP ČR) – member entry for Česká fintech asociace / odvětvové svazy
why_relevant: SP ČR republishes affiliated sector associations' profiles including enumerated member companies — this page carried an explicit fintech member roster (AKCENTA, BONDSTER, ComGate, GOPAY, MONET+, Twisto, Zentity …). Acts as a second, independently-maintained copy of association rosters and a hub to other 'odvětvové svazy'.

source_name: SP ČR – Abecední seznam členů (alphabetical member base)
why_relevant: Largest CZ employers' federation; the alphabetical roster mixes large corporates and sector unions, so it broadens the supplier/buyer map beyond finance-only associations (IT integrators, telco, security printing). Companion 'jmenný seznam kontaktů' gives named representatives useful for actor mapping.

source_name: ICT UNIE – Členové ICTU (ICT supplier directory)
source_subtype: association member directory with outbound links
why_relevant: 51 regular + 9 honorary members, listed A–Ž with hyperlinks to each company site — the core roster of ICT integrators bidding on Czech public and banking IT tenders (Asseco CE, Atos, AutoCont, České Radiokomunikace, Dell, IBM, Huawei…). Directly answers 'who are the likely bidders/competitors on a given award notice'. English mirror at /en/ictu-members.

source_name: ICT UNIE – Pracovní skupiny (working groups)
why_relevant: Working groups (eGovernment, kybernetická bezpečnost, veřejné zakázky) reveal which vendors organise around which state procurement themes — a cheap proxy for which suppliers are positioning for upcoming public IT/payment tenders.

source_name: Asociace pro veřejné zakázky (AVZ) – Členové AVZ
why_relevant: The single most on-topic association for workstream A2: AVZ segments its members into zadavatelé (contracting authorities), dodavatelé (suppliers), administrátoři/poradci and advokátní kanceláře. That segmentation is effectively a ready-made buyer/supplier/intermediary map for Czech public procurement, including municipalities that run tenders.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách (MMR) – Partneři page listing AVZ
why_relevant: The ministry procurement portal's partner page confirms which professional bodies are institutionally recognised in CZ procurement, and links onward to them — a credible pointer for association discovery and legitimacy scoring. (URL observed as http and may redirect to portal-vz.gov.cz.)

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) – členové / členské banky
why_relevant: The Czech card-payments body: ~18 regular members (financial institutions only) plus ~23 observers, and its statistics pages enumerate contributing issuers/acquirers including non-banks (EVO Payments, Euronet, CCS, Twisto, Essox). For POS/card-terminal procurement this is the precise buyer list. Note two domains in circulation: bankovnikarty.cz (institutional) and bankovni-karty.cz (content).

source_name: Asociace poskytovatelů platebních služeb ČR (ASPPS)
why_relevant: Dedicated payment-service-provider association (IČO 04387783, founded 2015) whose stated role is representing PSP interests before ministries and regulators. Even a small roster is high-signal for payments-sector supplier/buyer mapping. Membership list was NOT visible in search results — needs a direct site crawl to confirm whether a members page exists.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci, Seznam členů
why_relevant: ~580 e-commerce companies, software vendors and financial institutions. For payments this is the merchant-side demand map (who buys payment gateways, POS, BNPL) plus the certified-shop directory at certifikovany-obchod.cz. A member-only zone exists, so part of the directory may be gated.

source_name: SPIR – Sdružení pro internetový rozvoj, Členové
why_relevant: Internet-economy roster including banks as members (ČSOB observed), media, adtech and technology vendors (Adform, SAS Institute ČR, Seznam.cz, RTB House). Weaker for tenders than ICT UNIE/AVZ but useful for mapping digital-marketing and data suppliers that banks procure from. Legacy English member list exists at old.spir.cz.

source_name: AKAT ČR – Členové asociace (capital market)
why_relevant: Investment companies, foreign fund managers and service providers active in CZ collective investment. Extends the financial-buyer universe beyond banks/leasing into asset management, which procures custody, reporting and payments infrastructure. A historical merged-member list is also archived on the site.

source_name: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP) – Řádní členové
why_relevant: 25 insurers covering >98% of the CZ insurance market. Insurers are adjacent financial buyers of the same core-systems, payments and document-output vendors as banks, and several are bancassurance arms of ČBA members — useful for group-level buyer resolution. Archive mirror at archiv.cap.cz preserves older rosters; English section exists.

source_name: Hospodářská komora ČR (komora.cz) – členská základna / oborová sdružení
why_relevant: ~17,000 members organised in 57 territorial chambers and ~140 industry associations. The value is the association index (a master pointer to further sector bodies) and the regional chambers' own member catalogues; a single national supplier catalogue was not located from the surface web, so this is a hub-of-hubs rather than one list.

source_name: AMSP ČR – Členská základna (SMEs and collective members)
why_relevant: Membership base is largely collective (guilds, cechy, clusters, professional associations) — which makes it a snowball engine for discovering further niche associations rather than a company list. Relevant for finding SME-side suppliers and the retail-merchant lobby that shapes POS/payments policy.

source_name: Svaz měst a obcí ČR + regional unions (SMO ČR / SMOJK) – member municipality lists
why_relevant: Municipalities are the highest-volume contracting authorities in CZ public procurement, including for cash handling, POS/e-payment for local fees and IT. Regional unions publish itemised member lists (SMOJK: 131 members as of Aug 2025); the national SMO ČR site did not surface an open itemised roster, so regional unions plus the RÚIAN/ARES obce registries are the practical route.

source_name: CACIO – Česká asociace manažerů IT
why_relevant: ~101 senior IT executives (including from banks) as individual members. Its member roster appears not to be published, so value is in event programmes and the CACIO fórum agendas, which name the organisations and decision-makers steering IT investment — an actor-map source rather than a directory.
